title: Regional tier-aware soft-fail orchestrator and adaptive circuit heuristics
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Implement a region- and tier-aware ‘soft-fail’ orchestration layer that automatically trips circuit breakers and triggers fallback routing to compatible model variants (lower-cost/quantized models, sibling regions, or cached prefixes) when preconfigured operational signals cross adaptive thresholds. This ticket covers the detection heuristics, circuit state machine, integration points with the routing service, feature-flagged rollout, and monitoring + playbook. The design must balance aggressive protection of capacity and SLOs with minimal false positives to avoid unnecessary degradation for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Detector observes 429 rate, request timeouts, 5xx error-rate, and p95 latency on a per-region-per-tier basis and emits decisions to the routing service
Circuit breaker implements Closed/Open/Half-Open states with exponential backoff and jitter; half-open probes limited to a small cross-section of traffic
Fallback actions supported: route to lower-tier model variant, route to alternate region, return cached prefix response (if applicable), or apply client-visible 429 with Retry-After when appropriate
Feature-flag controlled rollout with canary and % rollouts; automated rollback when blocked by safety thresholds
End-to-end tests validate behavior under synthetic overload (burst 429s, sustained p95 increases, and region outage) in staging
Dashboards and alerts: 429 surge alerts, circuit-open rate, and number of fallback activations per customer; runbook documented
technical_notes: We will compute signals on a 60s sliding window with sub-buckets (6 x 10s) to capture bursts and sustained trends
Two-tier 429 detection: immediate-burst detector (burst_429_count >= X within 10s) and sustained-429 detector (rate > 3% over 60s) to differentiate throttling vs transient spikes
Timeout-based trigger: rolling p95 latency above threshold (configurable per model: default 1200ms) for 60s will start degradation path
Error-rate trigger: 5xx error-rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes => escalate to open circuit for minimal hold time
Circuit open duration uses exponential backoff: open_ms = min(base_ms * 2^n + jitter, max_ms). base_ms default 30000, max_ms default 900000. n increments on successive opens for same routing key
Half-open probing: send at most 0.5% of traffic or 10 qps (whichever smaller) through for a 30s probe window; success if error-rate < configured_success_rate and p95 < configured_latency

Routing spill logic: prefer cross-region sibling with preserved model architecture (same tokenizer) to avoid semantic regressions; otherwise fallback to compatible quantized variant of same model family
Back-pressure vs early-fallback: when queue depth on serving GPU exceeds configured high-water mark, prefer immediate fallback rather than queueing to protect latency SLOs
Feature flagging and gating hooks inside routing-service: evaluate detector decisions (allowlist/denylist per-customer), opt-out for enterprise dedicated tenants

Resource impact: detector runs in the routing plane; ensure it's bounded CPU (profiling target) and does not add caller-per-request latency >2ms. Consider offloading heavy math to a worker with async signals if needed
tasks: Implement detector and circuit state machine in routing-service (RFC + PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4821)
Integrate fallback model registry lookup and cross-region compatibility checks
Add feature flag and rollout toggle; implement canary % ramp in console
Add unit tests, integration test harness for synthetic overload, and chaos test for region loss
Create dashboards (Grafana) and alert rules (PagerDuty/Slack) and draft runbook
Staging validation and phased production rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback criteria
risks_mitigations: False positives: Tune detectors with conservative defaults and provide an initial long cooldown; add telemetry to track false-open events and auto-adjust thresholds
Semantic regression from fallback model: Add safety net to only route to models with validated equivalence level; include fallback opt-out per-route for critical customers
Oscillation between regions: Introduce sticky dampening windows and cooldown per routing key to prevent flapping
Cost spike when routing to larger/replicated capacity: Enforce per-tenant budget caps and require approval for cross-region cost fallbacks
Operational complexity: Start with a single region/tier pair as pilot and add metrics to track MTTR for circuit incidents
